name_note: The GTDB genus matches the genus Porphyromonas used in the literature; GTDB additionally places one genome labelled Falsiporphyromonas in it.

sentences.text: Porphyromonas is a bacterial genus whose members are distributed across sites of the human oral cavity in health and disease.

A metagenomic study of nine oral sites reported site-specific distribution patterns, ecotype differentiation and metabolic specialization across Porphyromonas taxa, with Porphyromonas pasteri the most abundant taxon in healthy subjects.
The same study reported that Porphyromonas gingivalis was rare in healthy subjects but present in periodontal disease, and that Porphyromonas catoniae was restricted to healthy dental plaque.

Published work describes the mouth as an important reservoir for respiratory pathogens and for oral microbes including Porphyromonas, and reports lung microbiome biogeography as balanced between oral-pharyngeal microaspiration and clearance.
A study reported that Porphyromonas was significantly enriched in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, including oral squamous cell carcinoma tissues.
